Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall tonight
or early tomorrow on the Northern Gulf Coast near Alabama or Florida.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports it's currently a Category 2 storm with winds of 110 miles
per hour.
Forecasters with the National Hurricane Center say this will be a dangerous hurricane at
landfall, with winds topping 100 miles an hour, life-threatening storm surge between
five and seven feet, and rainfall up to 15 inches in some areas.
Local officials have ordered evacuations along some Florida panhandle beaches and have open
shelters.
Alabama ordered tourists to leave its coast.
More than half of the offshore oil and gas production in the Gulf has been curtailed
according to the Marine Minerals Administration.
Isaias has been rapidly gaining strength from the warm waters of the Gulf.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Crestview, Florida.
For the second time this week, Saudi Arabia says its airport in the capital, Riyadh, was
targeted.
Three people were killed, two more people died earlier this week in similar attacks.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports the killings are from Houthi missile attacks.
Saudi Arabia says three Saudi citizens, including a commercial pilot, were killed and a number
of people wounded in attacks on Thursday that targeted Riyadh's international airport.
Saudi Arabia's aviation authority says the attacks struck a Saudi aircraft and a building.
It's at least the third time this week that Houthi missiles pierced through Saudi air
defenses, killing and wounding people at Riyadh airport and another airport in the south.
Yemen's Houthis say they're targeting Saudi air bases and airports in response to hundreds
of Saudi airstrikes this week on Yemen that they say have killed and wounded people there.
The U.N. says the fighting in Yemen between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and the
Iran-backed Houthis has displaced nearly 200,000 people.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize is former U.N. human rights chief and international
jurist Navi Pillay.
She led a U.N. inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory.
The Israeli foreign ministry has condemned the choice, saying that the Nobel Committee
has rewarded the biggest lie of the 21st century.
President Trump says the United States won't be attacking Iran at any time before the midterm
U.S. elections.
And Piers Domenico Montanaro says President Trump made the announcement on social media.
The reality is more strikes and further engagement is a tough sell for an American audience, including
for many in Trump's base.
I mean, Trump explicitly promised to not get into foreign entanglements.
He even said in his inaugural that his presidency might be measured by the wars he didn't get
into.
The prolonged unpopular wars we know can be and have been dangerous for any president
and his party.
This is NPR.
In Alaska last night, the state's gubernatorial candidates held a debate.
The contest is a four-way ranked choice race under Alaska's unique voting system.
Alaska Public Media's Eric Stone reports the current governor is term-limited.
Three Republicans are facing off against a Democrat in the race to be Alaska's next governor.
Democrat Jonathan Christ Tompkins has a lead over the fractured Republican field.
He's positioning himself as a pragmatic moderate.
We need to be able to work together to find common ground, to bridge where there's disagreement,
and that's what's going to move Alaska forward.
The top polling Republican is business owner Bernadette Wilson.
She said she'd fight efforts to raise taxes on oil companies as Alaska stares down a budget
crunch.
I am up for that battle.
I do not want a governor that's going to concede the fight before they even get started.
Several recent polls show the Democrat winning as voters sour on President Trump and Alaska's
incumbent Republican governor.
For NPR News, I'm Eric Stone in Anchorage.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the U.S. military will show the execution of a condemned
man by firing squad.
Hegseth says Nidal Hassan's death will be live-streamed in early December.
Hassan killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009.
People in France say two stolen paintings by Renoir have been located.
They've been taken from a museum in southern France.
The mayor of the town says six people allegedly connected with the heist have also been arrested.
The paintings were the portrait of Madame Colonna Romano and the young woman at the
well.
